key_insight: Multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated psychiatric intake improved clinical interviewing, diagnostic reasoning, and communication, with gains transferring to psychiatrist-enacted encounters.
engineering_relevance: Simulation offers a controlled testbed for training and stress-testing conversational agents before clinician-supervised use.
method: Train a language model with multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated psychiatric intake.
Compare against its identically prompted base model in a randomized, double-blind crossover study.
Stress-test safety using 256 adversarial presentations derived from Delphi-consensus taxonomies.
evidence_signal: Across 60 matched scenario pairs (120 psychiatrist-enacted encounters), the trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of pairs (p < 0.0001); adversarial testing found acute-risk under-triage fell from 30.5% to 12.9%.
watch_item: Evaluation used simulated and psychiatrist-enacted encounters rather than real patient care; residual safety failures require safeguards and clinician oversight.
paper_title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
